items.q: A 64-year-old man has buttock and thigh cramps after two streets with weak femoral pulses. Imaging shows focal bilateral common iliac stenoses. Which first-line logic best suits short focal aortoiliac narrowings with buttock claudication?
o: Endovascular stenting first for focal TASC A-B lesions
Open bypass for every short stenosis
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Endovascular stenting first for focal TASC A-B lesions.** Short focal iliac narrowings open durably with stents where surgery overshoots.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Bypass overshoots focal disease
- C: Claudication deserves treatment
- D: Amputation never treats claudication
**Key point:** Focal iliac disease stents first.
items.kp: Focal aortoiliac narrowings suit endovascular first.
